ny_the_pump_factory.blurb: The Pump Factory is the steep left-hand end of the Main Face at Beaver Brook, a rare sport-climbing cliff in the Adirondacks near Wilmington. Twelve routes, nearly all bolted, climb overhanging pale grey rock that is known for sustained forearm pump. The grades run from a single 5.8 up into the 5.12s, with most of the lines in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits stronger sport climbers more than beginners. Falls are clean and the bolting is generous, and a stick clip helps on some starts. It catches plenty of sun, which makes it a good cool-weather choice, while bugs can be a nuisance in warm months.
ny_the_pump_factory.parking_note: Leave the car at the small pull-off on Hardy Road in Wilmington, which is also used by mountain bikers.
ny_the_pump_factory.approach: Walk west along the trail for about a third of a mile to a cairn on the right, then turn uphill through the forest, keeping right of the rocky gully and following the base of the cliff band. Allow roughly 15 to 20 minutes.

ny_rec_center_boulder.blurb: Rec Center Boulder is a city boulder on the north side of Marcus Garvey Park in Harlem, near the pool and looking over the open lawn. It holds a dozen problems on slabs, and most are easy to moderate, from V0 up to about V4. The footholds are small and polished, so the climbing relies on trusting friction, and anyone new to slab may find it a couple of grades stiffer than the numbers suggest. Topouts are tall for the city, so bring pads and a spotter. It is a handy after-work spot rather than a destination, and the park has other small boulders nearby.

ny_headrush_boulder.blurb: Headrush Boulder is one of the bigger blocks in the Moby Area at Ice Pond, a bouldering park near Brewster in Putnam County. A dozen problems cover a wide spread, from an easy V1 warm-up through a cluster of V3 to V4 lines and a few hard ones reaching about V8. Besides face climbing there is some crack and off-width work, and a cave on the left side holds a short sit-start roof problem that is worth two or three pads. The boulder sits just off the main trail, a short stroll past a neighbouring named block, so it fits easily into a circuit of the Moby Area.

ny_rogers_slide.blurb: Rogers Slide is a big slab of roughly 700 feet that drops straight into the water at the north end of Lake George, near Hague. The twelve routes are mostly traditional multi-pitch lines of two to four pitches, with a pair of bolted lines, and the grades stay friendly, from 5.5 to 5.8. That makes it a classic moderate day for newer leaders, though the climbing is serious in scale. You reach the base by boat, so the day starts with paddling or a ferry, and you should plan for strong summer sun on the face and carry two ropes for the rappels.

ny_stewarts_ledge.blurb: Stewarts Ledge is a short-walk cliff on the east side of Lake George, reached from the Buck Mountain trailhead in the Fort Ann area. It holds a dozen lines mixing trad, sport and top-rope, ranging from easy 5.6 climbs through plenty of 5.9 and 5.10 up to a single 5.11. The rock is good along the main climbs but turns loose on either side, so stay within the cleaner stretch. With a quick approach on a worn path along the base, it works well for an after-work session. Lake George climbers rate late spring and autumn as the prime windows, because early spring can leave seepage.
ny_stewarts_ledge.parking_note: Use the Buck Mountain trailhead on Pilot Knob Road near Fort Ann; the lot fills up on nice days.

ny_rookie_boulder.blurb: Rookie Boulder is a large glacial block in the Green Lake Boulders group in the southern Adirondacks, and it is the first boulder you meet on the walk in from the Kane Mountain trailhead. Its slightly overhanging wall holds twelve problems that run from an easy V0 up to a single V9, with a decent middle of V2 to V5 lines. That spread makes it friendly for a mixed group. The area dries slowly and can seep for days after rain, though most problems are usually fine after two or three dry days, and the humid, still air means bugs in season.
ny_rookie_boulder.parking_note: Park at the Kane Mountain trailhead, where the short walk to the boulders begins.
ny_rookie_boulder.approach: Walk back toward Green Lake Road, cross the small culvert, then bear right over a little stream; the boulders are a couple of hundred yards further on.

ny_b_the_playground.blurb: The Playground is the second section of the Dickie Barre cliff on the Peterskill side of the Shawangunks, a newer area with mostly trad lines, some of which also work as top-ropes. It starts at a pair of tall white pines and continues right to a large, imposing roof that so far has only projects. The dozen climbs range from easy 5.5 and 5.6 lines through 5.8 and 5.9 up to a few 5.10s, so there is something for most leaders. A 60 foot static rope is often handy for anchors, and the cliff is a short walk from the road.
